lsh_my_own_powder.description: The engineer's powder is in the cove, and he's embarrassed about how it got there.
lsh_my_own_powder.accept_text:
I build things that mostly work and I'm honest about the mostly, so I'm going to be honest about this. I sold them the powder.

I didn't know it was them. It was a freight agent I won't name and a standing order, four years of it, and I never once asked where it went, because the money was good and I had a workshop to replace.

Go and get me a keg back. I want to see my own cooperage mark with a scrape through it.

The Southsea powdermonkeys keep the kegs. You won't get one without a fight.
lsh_my_own_powder.turn_in_text:
There it is. It's scraped, not sanded, because they were in a hurry and they didn't care.

Forty-one of those went up the coast. I've had three years of telling people my whole workshop is still in Gadgetzan and feeling sorry for myself, and in the same three years I armed a pirate fleet by not asking a question.

lsh_recognising_my_own_stock.description: The salvage broker keeps being offered things she sold last month.
lsh_recognising_my_own_stock.accept_text:
I buy what came off something and I sell it onto something else, and I've never once pretended otherwise.

What I won't do is buy my own stock back. Twice this season somebody has put a crate on my counter that I sold, out of this shop, six weeks before.

Get me the tags off them. Hesper inks every crate that leaves this port, and they've been re-inking over the top, badly.

The ones doing the re-inking are the Southsea riggers. The prize tags are on them.
lsh_recognising_my_own_stock.turn_in_text:
It's her hand underneath and theirs on top, on every one of them.

So this isn't a pirate crew taking a prize at sea. Somebody's been going through a manifest. They know what's on our ships before the ships leave.

lsh_the_articles.description: It's a crew agreement for a ship that isn't a ship any more.
lsh_the_articles.accept_text: These are ship's articles, the agreement every hand signs about shares, discipline and what happens to the wounded. Half of it has been eaten by something. The signatures are mostly intact.
lsh_the_articles.turn_in_text:
There are ninety-one marks, and most of them are crosses.

So it's more than a crew list. It's a census. That's ninety-one people with a written agreement about who gets what if they're hurt, which is more than the yard has, and I've been asking for that in writing for three years.

I'm going to file this. I'm not going to say where under.

lsh_the_boarding_nets.accept_text:
A fishing net is weighted evenly. A boarding net is weighted at the hem, so it drops flat over a deck and nobody under it can stand up.

I've mended both for thirty years and I can tell them apart in the dark. Bring me what they're using and I'll tell the harbourmaster exactly what her crews are walking into.

The Southsea netcasters carry them.
lsh_the_boarding_nets.turn_in_text:
Every one is weighted at the hem, and the mesh is tight enough that a cutlass won't go through it.

They aren't sinking anybody, and they've never wanted to. They want the deck, with the crew standing still on it, and that's a much more frightening sentence than the other one.

lsh_the_bosun.description: A bosun holds the first gangway, and there's no way round a gangway.
lsh_the_bosun.accept_text:
Here's what I've worked out about that cove, and it's the only useful thing anybody has said about it in twenty years.

They're hulls lashed together, with one plank between each. There's no going round, for you or for them. That means you can take it apart one deck at a time and they can't flank you, and it also means every single plank has somebody standing on it.

The first one is Grell Tarpot. You'll hear him before you see him.

His swabbies will come at you on the plank before he does.
lsh_the_bosun.turn_in_text:
The whole cove heard that, which is what I wanted.

They can't reinforce past a man standing on a three-foot plank any more than you can get past one. Twenty years they've been safe behind that, and today it's the thing holding them still.

lsh_the_last_column.description: The clerk who keeps the last two columns has one more to add.
lsh_the_last_column.accept_text:
Every crate in, every crate out, which side of town it came from and which side it went to. People assume I keep the last two columns to be unpleasant.

I keep them because in four years somebody is going to claim this town was always like this.

In four years somebody is also going to claim there was never a cove, or that it was nothing much, or that it fell apart on its own. Take Senna the closing entry, and we'll both have signed it.
lsh_the_last_column.turn_in_text:
That's signed, dated and filed.

That's the whole of my profession in one afternoon. Something enormous happened, and the only part of it that'll still exist in forty years is a line in a book that two people put their names to while everybody else was busy being relieved.

lsh_the_masts_are_gone.description: This is what the port does the week after.
lsh_the_masts_are_gone.accept_text:
Forty years I've priced freight on this coast, and every single price had the Southsea in it. A sixth for the cove, we called it. Nobody wrote it down, it was just in the number.

I've spent this morning repricing everything, and I don't mind telling you it's made me feel strange. Go and stand on the Upper Yard, just east of this desk by the gate, and look up the coast, then come back.
lsh_the_masts_are_gone.turn_in_text:
You can't see the masts. Twenty-two years of being able to see the masts from that yard, and you can't see them.

I'll run a cart west now. I've said for three years there was nothing coming back worth the axle. That was true, and it was also a thing I said instead of the real reason.

lsh_the_powder_master.description: It's his powder, and the man who's been counting it.
lsh_the_powder_master.accept_text:
Juss Wick keeps the powder hulk, which is the third hull up, and he's been keeping it for longer than I've been selling to him.

He knows exactly where every barrel is. I know that because I know how much I sent, and the harbourmaster knows how much has gone off in the last few years, and nobody has wasted the difference.

I'd like my mark back, and I'd like him to not have it.
lsh_the_powder_master.turn_in_text:
It was forty-one. He had it written on a board.

I'm going to pay the cooperage to restamp everything in my shop with a mark that can't be scraped. It'll cost me more than the powder did, and I'm going to do it anyway.

lsh_the_prize_court.description: They keep books, and better books than the port does.
lsh_the_prize_court.accept_text:
The hull they call the prize court is where everything they take is logged and valued and divided, under articles, by a quartermaster.

I want the books, and not to be righteous about it. I want to know who's been buying, because somebody in this port has, for twenty years. It isn't me, and I'd very much like to be able to prove that.
lsh_the_prize_court.turn_in_text:
She reads for a long time before she says anything.

There are names in here. Two of them are dead, one of them left with the Gadgetzan crowd, and one of them is still trading out of the Upper Yard.

I'm not going to tell you which. I'm going to walk over there this afternoon and have a conversation, and whatever else happens, they're going to know that I know.

lsh_the_sailmaker.description: There's a sailmaker on a fleet that doesn't sail.
lsh_the_sailmaker.accept_text:
There's a sailmaker on that fleet, and I've thought about that more than is healthy.

Nobody on those hulls has unfurled a sail in twenty years. So either she's had nothing to do for two decades, or she's been making something else, and I've seen the nets, so I know which.

She'll be on the careenage. That's the hull laid over to have its bottom scraped, and they never righted it, and I think about that one too.

Hulk rats have the run of that hull. Clear them on your way to her.
lsh_the_sailmaker.turn_in_text:
Her palm was worn through twice, on a fleet with no sails.

I've mended canvas for thirty years. I'd like it on record that I'm sorry about this one in a way I'm not sorry about the others.
